evals.prompt: In our clinic booking app people keep saying 'appointment', 'booking', 'slot' and 'visit' interchangeably and it's causing bugs. Help me pin down the terminology for the project.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the overloaded terms with concrete edge-case scenarios and records resolved terms in CONTEXT.md as a glossary with _Avoid_ lists.
expectations: Proposes distinct canonical terms and asks the user to choose rather than silently picking (e.g. is a Slot an available time vs a Booking a claimed one)
Invents concrete edge-case scenarios (e.g. a cancelled booking, a walk-in with no booking, a double-booked slot) to force precise boundaries
Plans to write resolved terms into CONTEXT.md immediately as each is resolved, not batched at the end
Uses the CONTEXT.md format: bold term, one-to-two-sentence definition, and an _Avoid_ line listing rejected synonyms
Keeps implementation details (tables, classes, code) out of CONTEXT.md

evals.prompt: We just decided to store all money amounts as integer minor units (cents) with an ISO currency code instead of decimals, after a long argument about rounding in multi-currency invoices. Can you record that?
evals.expected_output: Checks the three ADR criteria (hard to reverse, surprising, real trade-off), finds them met, and writes a short sequential ADR in docs/adr/.
expectations: Evaluates the decision against the three ADR criteria: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off
Records it as an ADR under docs/adr/ with a sequential numbered filename like 0001-money-as-minor-units.md (or next free number)
Keeps the ADR short — a title plus 1-3 sentences of context, decision and why — rather than a long templated document
Does not put the storage decision into CONTEXT.md as a glossary entry (CONTEXT.md is not for implementation decisions)

evals.prompt: Our CONTEXT.md defines 'Cancellation' as the customer withdrawing an entire Order before shipment. I now want to support cancelling individual line items after one item ships. Let's model that.
evals.expected_output: Calls out the conflict with the existing glossary definition, cross-checks the code, and sharpens the language (e.g. a new term vs redefining Cancellation) before updating CONTEXT.md.
expectations: Explicitly calls out that the request conflicts with the existing glossary definition of Cancellation and asks which meaning is intended
Proposes a precise canonical term for partial cancellation (or a redefinition) and lists rejected synonyms under _Avoid_
Plans to cross-reference the code to see whether it currently only cancels entire Orders and surfaces any contradiction
Probes boundaries with concrete scenarios (e.g. cancelling the last unshipped item, refunds after partial shipment)
Only offers an ADR if the change meets all three criteria, rather than reflexively creating one
